scenes.title: Utility-Based Agents & Workflow
scenes.voiceover_narration: The third type is the utility-based agent. A utility-based agent goes further than goal-based reasoning. It doesn't just ask, will this action achieve the goal? It asks, which available action achieves the goal most efficiently, at the lowest cost, and with the highest confidence. At Solara, a utility-based agent managing report generation across hundreds of sites needs to make trade-off decisions constantly. Do I generate a full diagnostic report or a summary? Do I escalate the anomaly or log it for review? It evaluates options against a utility function and picks the best one.

scenes.title: Handoff, Summary & What's Next
scenes.voiceover_narration: Let's bring it together. Every agent is built from four components. Perception, memory, reasoning, and action working together in a continuous loop. That loop drives agent environment interaction. The agent observes, decides, acts, and observes again. The three types of agents, reactive, goal-based, and utility-based represent increasing levels of sophistication. Reactive agents are fast and rule-driven. Goal-based agents plan towards outcomes. Utility-based agents optimize across trade-offs.
